newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids mostly steady, crude, natgas slide.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids mostly steady, crude, natgas slide.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oi prices stayed little changed Tuesday in thin trade, but softer crude and gas markets again had some expecting resid to soon buckle, industry sources said.
"We're in pre-winter doldrums, and with gas coming off, you have to see lower numbers soon," said one cash trader.
But others said much of the fuel switching from resid to gas has already taken place, and tight high sulphur stocks could hold up the complex near-term.
New York Harbor prompt one percent was still quoted at $17.50 a barrel, with Sept paper also steady at $16.60-80.
NYH Oct one percent paper was unchanged at about $17, while November also was flat from Monday at $17.40-50. January quotes were in the $18.25 area, traders said.
High sulphurs in NYH notionally were steady, but traders said two 2.2 percent sales Monday at $16.15 and $16.75 (both delivered) showed the HSFO market was still relatively firm.

At the U.S. Gulf Coast, one percent was still at $16.25-50, with a piece reported done at $16.50 but details on the deal were not known. USG three percent held around $14.75. Traders said two prompt USG three percent barges sold Monday at $15.10 (FOB Houston) and $14.50 (FOB Miss. River).
New York city gate September gas prices fell five cents Tuesday to about $2.00/mmBtu area versus NYH one percent resid at a $2.77/mmBtu equivalent.
